claim: The audit pre-check ("a usage error must come before the workers of the review run") does not check that --models gives two or more distinct models, which cmd_verify requires. So `audit ... --models sonnet` runs init, targets and review (starting workers) and only then fails in verify.
what_goes_wrong: `hpflow audit --models sonnet` (or a repeated model) passes the pre-check, runs init, targets and the paid review workers, and only then fails in verify with 'verify needs two models or more', wasting the review cost.
fix_idea: In the audit pre-check, map the models to ids and apply the same checks as cmd_verify (at least two, no duplicates) before init.

claim: A SARIF result whose artifact uri is not a valid URL (for example 'file://[bad/x.py') makes urlsplit raise ValueError inside file_of_uri. outside.read does not catch it, so the whole import call crashes instead of skipping that one entry with a reason, as the module docstring promises.
what_goes_wrong: One SARIF result with a malformed artifact uri (e.g. 'file://[bad/x.py') makes urlsplit raise ValueError, so the whole import command crashes and no other finding in the file is imported.
fix_idea: Wrap file_of_uri in sarif_entries in try/except ValueError and append (None, 'the file address is not valid') for that result.
